housing starts have been over recent years. In 1976 we had
273,000	housing starts; in 1977 we had 246,000 housing starts; in 1978 we had 228,000; in 1979 we had 197,000; in 1980, 158,000; and in 1981 we had 178,000 housing starts.
The minister can stand in this House and tell us how many jobs he is going to create. It is quite possible he will create many jobs if he brings the housing industry to a complete stop and then turns around and brings in legislation saying it will help the housing industry and will increase employment. Unfortunately, the housing industry does not agree; the industry suggests that 50,000 housing units are needed to bring up employment in the construction industry and that there will be 100,000 jobs lost, not gained, by this bill. That is reflected in about $2.8 billion lost to the construction industry, which translates into $400 million lost revenue to the government. Yet this minister insists on suggesting that he is going to increase employment.
In 1981 the average home sold for $61,000, which is 12 per cent higher than the previous year. The Minister of Finance (Mr. MacEachen) then has the gall to stand in this House and say that people are doing well because the average income of a person buying a home is $36,658, an increase of 22 per cent over the previous year. His answer is that if incomes are up by that amount, more people must be able to buy homes. However, CMHC suggests that fewer people were able to buy a home in 1981 than in 1980. The age of the average purchaser went from 30 to 32. The proportion of buyers who were previous home owners rose from 39 per cent to 56 per cent. Surely the Minister of Finance (Mr. MacEachen) and the Minister of Public Works have more common sense than to suggest that home buyers are better able to buy homes at these new prices.
At second reading, the NDP suggested that the increased price of homes was due to the increase in the price of land. Statistics for the last year indicate that the average price of land remained constant. Therefore, that is not the reason for the increase in price. It was due to the high interest rates and nothing more.
I have asked the Minister of Public Works questions in this House. There are more questions I would have liked to ask. Why is the government spending $60 million on advertising which could be used to help home owners and renters in this country? Can the Minister of Public Works tell us why foreign aid will be increased by 19.9 per cent, or by $157 million, in the coming year when this money could have been used for home owners and renters?
Can the minister tell us why more is not done about Crown corporations which continue to lose money? Eldorado Nuclear is losing $130 million, yet it was hiring people on the day it closed its mine last fall. In spite of this the minister has the gall to tell us he is doing all he can to help home owners and renters in this country.
From time to time members opposite have asked what we would do. We have many, many suggestions. I will mention just a few. We would encourage, not discourage, investment capital in this country. In the last two years $17 billion has left this country because of the energy policies of this government.
There is an excess of natural gas in western Canada. It has been estimated that up to $2 billion in sales could accrue by the export of this natural gas. What does the government do? It discourages exports. It discourages the development of the oil industry in western Canada. It is discouraging one of the few viable industries left in Canada. The government is attempting to do what it has done to the automobile industry, and we all know the terrible state of that industry.
This bill will do little. It is like giving an aspirin to someone who has an ulcer. It may help the pain just a little, but it will certainly not cure the problem. It does not deal with the real problem of high interest rates. However little the bill provides, we unfortunately must support it. However, we will continue to press the government for better legislation to bring needed help to both the home owner and the renter.
